authoritative_sources.title: Guidelines for the Provision of Echocardiography in Canada
authoritative_sources.issuing_organization: Canadian Cardiovascular Society and Canadian Society of Echocardiography
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: The CCS guideline library retains the Canadian echocardiography provision guideline. No newer CCS tumour-specific diagnostic guideline was identified; this packet uses it only for the investigation boundary.

supported_recommendations.statement: A patient with positional obstructive symptoms, embolic phenomena, or constitutional symptoms and a suspected intracardiac mass requires echocardiographic characterization and specialist assessment; atrial myxoma is a key diagnostic consideration.

source_citations.locator: Indications for echocardiography: assessment of cardiac masses and follow-up after surgical removal of masses/tumours

important_contraindications_or_exception.statement: A cardiac mass on imaging is not synonymous with myxoma; thrombus, vegetation, and other primary or metastatic lesions remain diagnostic alternatives.

source_citations.locator: Indications for echocardiographic assessment of cardiac masses

evidence_boundaries.statement: This packet supports recognition and diagnostic imaging of a suspected cardiac mass only; it does not encode surgical approach, pathology, or oncologic treatment.

evidence_notes: Bounded to recognition of a possible cardiac tumour and echocardiographic assessment.

authoritative_sources.title: Canadian Cardiovascular Society Consensus Conference 2004 on the Management of Valvular Heart Disease
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: CCS continues to host this Canadian consensus document. It is used only for stable recognition and echocardiographic characterization, not for intervention thresholds.

supported_recommendations.statement: A pathologic murmur or symptoms compatible with valve disease should be evaluated with echocardiography to characterize the affected valve, lesion severity, ventricular response, and associated hemodynamic consequences.

source_citations.locator: Diagnostic assessment and echocardiographic evaluation sections

important_contraindications_or_exception.statement: Murmur intensity alone does not establish valve-lesion severity; clinical findings require echocardiographic correlation.

source_citations.locator: Diagnostic reporting and echocardiographic assessment sections

evidence_boundaries.statement: This packet covers recognition of major stenotic and regurgitant lesions and confirmatory imaging, not procedure-selection or timing thresholds.

evidence_notes: No current procedural recommendation is extracted from this legacy Canadian consensus.

source_citations.locator: Diagnostic assessment and echocardiographic evaluation sections

authoritative_sources.title: Endocarditis: Diagnosis and Treatment
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: Emergency Care BC lists this as its current endocarditis clinical summary at retrieval.

supported_recommendations.statement: Suspected infective endocarditis should be assessed with blood cultures obtained before antimicrobial therapy when feasible and echocardiography; diagnosis integrates clinical, microbiological, and imaging evidence rather than a murmur alone.

source_citations.locator: Diagnosis section: critical diagnostic tests are blood cultures and echocardiography

important_contraindications_or_exception.statement: Negative blood cultures do not exclude infective endocarditis, particularly after prior antimicrobial exposure or with fastidious organisms.

source_family_target_assessments.rationale: No directly applicable current national Canadian specialty-society diagnostic guideline was located; Emergency Care BC provides current Canadian clinician-facing diagnostic guidance.

evidence_boundaries.statement: This packet supports recognition and initial diagnostic testing only; it does not prescribe antimicrobial regimens, duration, prophylaxis, or surgical indications.

evidence_notes: The Canadian provincial clinical source resolves the stable diagnostic claim without an international fallback.

authoritative_sources.title: Pediatric and Adolescent Care: Chapter 11, Cardiovascular System
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: The Canadian federal clinical manual remains publicly available and directly presents revised Jones criteria; no later national Canadian specialty-society rheumatic-fever diagnostic guideline was located.

supported_recommendations.statement: Diagnose a first episode of acute rheumatic fever by applying revised Jones criteria together with evidence of preceding group A streptococcal infection, using the risk-population definitions when interpreting articular and inflammatory findings.

source_citations.locator: Revised Jones' Criteria table and acute rheumatic fever section

important_contraindications_or_exception.statement: The revised Jones criteria vary between low-risk and high-risk populations; a compatible inflammatory syndrome without evidence of antecedent group A streptococcal infection does not establish a first episode.

source_family_target_assessments.rationale: No directly applicable current national Canadian specialty-society diagnostic guideline was located; the federal clinical manual provides the Canadian revised-Jones diagnostic framework.

evidence_boundaries.statement: This packet supports diagnostic recognition only and does not encode antimicrobial choice, anti-inflammatory therapy, or secondary-prophylaxis duration.

source_citations.locator: Acute rheumatic fever and revised Jones' Criteria sections

evidence_notes: Use the risk-stratified Canadian Jones-criteria table; no management recommendation is extracted.

authoritative_sources.title: 2017 Comprehensive Update of the Canadian Cardiovascular Society Guidelines for the Management of Heart Failure
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: CCS retains this comprehensive Canadian guideline; it is used for stable pericardial diagnostic recognition, not for an acute treatment algorithm.

supported_recommendations.statement: Acute pericarditis is suggested by a compatible inflammatory chest-pain syndrome with supportive examination, ECG, inflammatory-marker, or imaging findings; assess for important alternative causes of acute chest pain.

important_contraindications_or_exception.statement: Pleuritic or positional pain and diffuse ECG change do not by themselves exclude acute coronary syndrome, pulmonary embolism, myocarditis, or aortic disease when the presentation is concerning.

source_citations.locator: Pericardial disease diagnostic context in Chapter 7

evidence_boundaries.statement: This packet is limited to distinguishing a pericarditic presentation from competing chest-pain syndromes; it does not supply anti-inflammatory dosing or admission criteria.

authoritative_sources.title: 2017 Comprehensive Update of the Canadian Cardiovascular Society Guidelines for the Management of Heart Failure
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: CCS retains this comprehensive Canadian guideline; it is used only for the stable clinical recognition boundary between effusion and tamponade.

supported_recommendations.statement: A pericardial effusion becomes clinically urgent when there is evidence of tamponade physiology or hemodynamic compromise; bedside echocardiography helps identify effusion and its hemodynamic effects.

important_contraindications_or_exception.statement: The size of an effusion alone does not diagnose tamponade; integrate vital signs, clinical evidence of impaired filling, and echocardiographic physiology.

source_citations.locator: Pericardial disease diagnostic context in Chapter 7

evidence_boundaries.statement: This packet supports identification of tamponade physiology only and does not describe pericardiocentesis technique.

evidence_notes: The procedural do-not-test boundary is preserved.

authoritative_sources.title: 2017 Comprehensive Update of the Canadian Cardiovascular Society Guidelines for the Management of Heart Failure
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: The CCS guideline remains in the current library and has a dedicated constrictive-pericarditis diagnostic section.

supported_recommendations.statement: Consider constrictive pericarditis in otherwise unexplained right-heart-failure features, especially with prior pericardial disease or injury; use Doppler echocardiography and, when required, cross-sectional imaging or hemodynamic assessment to confirm constrictive physiology.

important_contraindications_or_exception.statement: Constrictive pericarditis can mimic other causes of right-heart failure; no single symptom, sign, or imaging finding should be used in isolation.

source_citations.locator: Chapter 7.2.3.2, clinical presentation and diagnostic evaluation

evidence_boundaries.statement: This packet supports clinical recognition and confirmation of constrictive physiology, not catheterization-tracing interpretation or pericardiectomy technique.

evidence_notes: Preserves the scope exclusion for detailed hemodynamic tracings.

authoritative_sources.title: Guidance Document: Product Monograph
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: Health Canada presents this as the current product-monograph guidance at retrieval.

supported_recommendations.statement: When evaluating an unexpected drug response, consider metabolic drug-drug, drug-food, transporter, and pharmacogenetic mechanisms; use the Canadian product monograph to identify clinically relevant interaction information for the specific drug.

source_citations.locator: Sections 9.4 Drug-drug interactions and 9.5 Drug-food interactions

important_contraindications_or_exception.statement: A pharmacokinetic interaction should not be assumed solely from shared CYP metabolism; the Canadian product monograph and patient-specific exposure, comorbidity, and medication context remain necessary.

source_citations.locator: Section 9.4: known and potential clinically relevant drug-drug interactions

source_family_target_assessments.rationale: Health Canada is the authoritative Canadian source for product-monograph interaction and pharmacokinetic information; no single current national specialty-society source covers the required medication-information boundary.

evidence_boundaries.statement: This packet supports mechanism-oriented recognition and safe source selection; it does not establish a fixed interaction list or dosing adjustment for a particular drug pair.

evidence_notes: Specific CYP examples must later be verified against the relevant current Canadian product monograph.

authoritative_sources.title: Canada Vigilance Program
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: Health Canada lists the current Canada Vigilance reporting program and healthcare-professional reporting resources at retrieval.

supported_recommendations.statement: Evaluate a suspected adverse drug reaction with a temporal medication history, including prescription, non-prescription, and natural-health products, and report suspected adverse reactions through the Canada Vigilance Program when reporting is indicated.

source_citations.locator: Canada Vigilance Program overview and health-professional reporting resources

important_contraindications_or_exception.statement: A Canada Vigilance report records a suspected adverse reaction and does not itself establish causality; alternative disease and medication explanations must still be assessed.

source_citations.locator: Program overview: suspected adverse-reaction reports and reporting tools

source_family_target_assessments.rationale: Health Canada operates the national Canada Vigilance pharmacovigilance and reporting pathway; it is the direct Canadian authority for the reporting portion of the packet.

evidence_boundaries.statement: The Canadian reporting pathway supports recognition and safety action but does not validate the Toronto Notes Type A-E classification as a current regulatory taxonomy.

evidence_notes: Classification labels are retained only as background organization; material claims are bounded to structured suspicion and Canadian reporting.

authoritative_sources.title: Guidance Document: Product Monograph
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: Health Canada presents this as the current product-monograph guidance at retrieval.

supported_recommendations.statement: Before prescribing a medication with potential interaction risk, reconcile all prescription, non-prescription, natural-health, and food exposures and consult the current Canadian product monograph for clinically relevant drug-drug and drug-food interactions.

source_citations.locator: Sections 9.4 Drug-drug interactions and 9.5 Drug-food interactions

important_contraindications_or_exception.statement: Do not infer that every co-administered drug creates a clinically meaningful interaction; the product-monograph evidence and patient-specific risk determine the safe response.

source_citations.locator: Section 9.4: known and potential clinically relevant drug-drug interactions

source_family_target_assessments.rationale: Health Canada product monographs are the direct Canadian regulatory source for product-specific interaction information and current safe-use comments.

evidence_boundaries.statement: This packet establishes the Canadian evidence source and interaction-recognition framework; it does not reproduce drug-pair-specific contraindications or dose-adjustment rules.

evidence_notes: Each future specific interaction claim must cite the applicable current Canadian product monograph.
